\section[el viajero]{el viajero — the traveller, the passenger}

\label{lesson:ES-C501-viajero}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the law, then the Spanish for freedom.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el viajero}
\textbf{el viajero} — \textquotedblleft{}the traveller, the passenger\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Los viajeros deben bajar del tren.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Passengers must get off the train.}
\end{quote}

A woman is \emph{la viajera}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el viajero}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el viajero}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el viajero}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the law, then the Spanish for freedom, then say \emph{el viajero} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el viajero mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The traveller, the passenger\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[conducir]{conducir — to drive}

\label{lesson:ES-C501-conducir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for freedom, then the Spanish for the traveller.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: conducir}
\textbf{conducir} — \textquotedblleft{}to drive\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Conduzco al trabajo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I drive to work.}
\end{quote}

It takes \emph{zc} in the first person present: \emph{conduzco}. In much of Latin America people say \emph{manejar}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[regresar]{regresar — to come back, to return}

Before the new one: say the Spanish for the traveller, then the Spanish for to drive.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: regresar}

\end{quote}

A close twin of \emph{volver}.

\section[la señal]{la señal — the sign, the signal}

\label{lesson:ES-C501-senal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to drive, then the Spanish for to come back.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la señal}
\textbf{la señal} — \textquotedblleft{}the sign, the signal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Sigue las señales hacia el aeropuerto.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Follow the signs to the airport.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Una señal de tráfico} — a road sign. \emph{No hay señal} — there is no signal, on a phone.
